column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṣakhr (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

“What I have forbidden you, avoid it; and what I have commanded you, do of it what you are able. For what destroyed those before you was only their excessive questions and their disagreeing with their prophets.” Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

Fa-jtanibūhu (“avoid it”): keep away from it. Istaṭaʿtum (“you are able”): you can manage. Man qablakum (“those before you”): the earlier nations. “Their disagreeing with their prophets”: their opposing their prophets.
The command to carry out what is commanded and avoid what is forbidden.
Prohibition is more stringent than command, because no allowance is made for committing any part of what is prohibited, whereas a command is restricted by ability.
Whoever is unable to do an obligation, or part of it, is excused what he is unable to do: “Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity” [al-Baqarah 2:286].

The prohibition of raising many questions in order to cause difficulty, out of affectation, or to stir up trouble about matters of the unseen or doubtful matters. As for asking about what befalls a person in his religious or worldly affairs, he must ask about it.
A warning to this nation against opposing its Prophet, as happened with the nations before it, lest they be destroyed as those were destroyed.

This hadith is one of the principles of the religion and one of the comprehensive statements. The Messenger ﷺ has shown us that when he forbids us something, we must avoid it entirely, without exception;

and when he commands us to do something, we should do of it what we can manage. He did not burden us with anything we are unable to do. This is part of the tolerance and ease of the religion, for Allah the Exalted does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.

Then he pointed to something like a parable as an admonition to us, that we should not be like some of the earlier nations, who asked their prophets many questions while opposing them, and so Allah punished them with various kinds of destruction and ruin; so let us not be like them and be destroyed as they were destroyed: “And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided” [Āl ʿImrān 3:103].
Beautiful patience! How near is relief! / Whoever is mindful of Allah in all matters is saved.
Whoever is true [to Him], no harm will reach him, / and whoever hopes in Him will find it where he hoped.
